By Roth’s theorem [10], \(\mu_{[1/2,1/2]}([n]) = o(1)\). See [2] for the best known upper bound for the size of a \((1/2,1/2)\)-sum free set. In [11, 12], instead of the form \(x+y=z\), Ruzsa instigated the study of more general linear equations \(a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=b\). In particular, for more general cases when \(p,q\) are positive integers and \(p \ge 2\), Hancock and Treglown [9] completely determined the value \(\mu_{[p,q]}([n])\). For higher dimensional lattices, Choi and Kim [5] initiated the investigation of the form \(x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_k=b\), where \(b\) is a prescribed points in \([n]^2\).
